intro.name: The proposal
intro.text: (Inventor) presents a proposal so peculiar that the village council cannot determine whether it is brilliant, foolish, or a joke.

idea1.text: Make a raft from tightly tied empty gourds.

idea2.text: Carry water uphill in a long chain of hollow reeds.

idea3.text: Train birds to deliver messages tied to their legs.

idea4.text: Build a bridge whose planks are suspended by woven vines.

idea5.text: Keep food cool in a shaded clay vessel surrounded by damp sand.

text_only.reason: the idea keeps food cool; no food is gained or lost

idea6.text: Use polished shells to reflect daylight into a dark hut.

idea7.text: Make a chair that follows its owner everywhere.

idea8.text: Teach fish to recognize the sound of a dinner bell.

idea9.text: Invent a spoon with a second spoon attached to it.

idea10.text: Plant every seed upside down to confuse the roots.

idea11.text: Construct a self-opening door that opens only when nobody approaches.

idea12.text: Paint the village's shadows to keep them from wandering away.

idea13.text: Create a hat large enough to shelter the entire village.

idea14.text: Replace all spoken greetings with an elaborate dance.

idea15.text: Build a cart with square wheels because circles are "overused."

idea16.text: Train snails to carry the harvest one grain at a time.

idea17.text: Invent a ceremonial bell that makes no sound.

idea18.text: Build a ladder that can be climbed from either end.

idea19.text: Store wind in sealed clay jars for a windless day.

idea20.text: Place a wooden sign reading "RAIN" beside the crops to encourage clouds.

choices.label: Give the inventor a modest budget and a safe trial.
Ask the inventor to defend the idea before the council.
Reject the proposal and invite a revised version.

a1.text:
IT WORKS:
The council is astonished. The idea solves a practical problem with ordinary materials, though the inventor's original explanation was nonsense. (Inventor) is offered a chance to teach the method.

a2.text:
IT SORT OF WORKS:
The device functions, but only under such specific conditions that it is scarcely useful. The villagers praise the effort and decline to build another.

a3.text:
THE ABSOLUTE FAILURE:
The project fails instantly. (Inventor) insists that the failure proves the idea is "ahead of its time." The council requests evidence.

a4.text:
THE UNEXPECTED SIDE EFFECT:
The device fails at its stated purpose but proves unexpectedly useful for {drying herbs|shading seedlings|teaching apprentices|decorating a festival}. (Inventor) accepts a small prize while continuing to insist the original idea was better.

a5.text:
THE GREAT LAUGH:
The entire audience assumes the proposal is comedy and applauds. (Inventor) is devastated to discover that nobody believed (inventor.him/her). A sympathetic elder offers to review the idea seriously.

b1.text:
THE GENIUS:
(Inventor) gives a clear demonstration and anticipates every objection. The council approves a supervised trial. The stern scholar grudgingly admits that appearances can deceive.

b2.text:
THE NONSENSE:
(Inventor) explains that the invention works because "everything wants to be somewhere else." The council asks for a testable explanation. (Inventor) offers a drawing of a smiling coconut.

b3.text:
THE INSULTED INVENTOR:
When the crowd laughs, (Inventor) shouts, "YOU LAUGHED AT MY LAST INVENTION TOO!" A builder replies, "Your last invention was a hole." "AN IMPROVED HOLE!" (Inventor) screams.

b4.text:
THE BETTER QUESTION:
A child asks what problem the invention solves. (Inventor) cannot answer. After a long silence, (inventor.he/she) admits that the invention was made simply to see whether it could be done.

b5.text:
THE COUNCIL IS STUMPED:
The leaders debate for hours and finally admit they cannot decide whether the invention is possible. They ask the researchers to test it rather than inventing a verdict.

c1.text:
THE QUIET COMEBACK:
(Inventor) returns weeks later with a smaller, more practical design. The council approves it. (Inventor) says nothing, but smiles broadly.

c2.text:
THE SPITEFUL MASTERPIECE:
(Inventor) spends months perfecting the rejected design. It works, but is still completely useless. The inventor demands a parade.

c3.text:
THE FORTY-SEVEN REVISIONS:
(Inventor) returns with forty-seven revised sketches. The leaders ask which one is best. "All of them," says (Inventor). The meeting ends abruptly.

c4.text:
THE LOST OPPORTUNITY:
A visiting artisan independently demonstrates the same useful principle months later. The council realizes it dismissed (Inventor) too quickly and apologizes.

c5.text:
THE FINAL WORD:
(Inventor) abandons the invention and returns to ordinary work. Years later, the village still jokes about it. (Inventor) finally laughs too, then admits that the ridicule hurt at the time.
